serialFormats.description: Bard (June 1980 to present): 3 digits, a letter, then the serial digits; the two digits immediately after the letter (positions 5-6) are the year of manufacture (98 = 1998). Month/week not encoded.
sources: Building Intelligence Center - Bard HVAC age (building-center.org/bard-hvac-age/)

Bard 'Coffee with Cliff' - New serial plate design (bardhvac.com, 2025)
notes: Three independent secondary decoders agree on the rule; not confirmed against a Bard warranty lookup, so confidence is capped at medium.
Examples are constructed to the published rule (year = digits 5-6); they were not taken from dated nameplate photos.
Pre-June-1980 Bard serials (6 digits + 2 letters, second letter = year, B = 1962) and the Apr-May 1980 11-character style are not decoded here; use the data plate date.

Since 2025 Bard prints the serial information as three separate fields on the data plate instead of one string - the year digits are still the two digits after the letter. A date printed on the plate always outranks this decode.

serialFormats.description: Nordyne / Nortek Global HVAC (Intertherm, Miller, Maytag, Frigidaire, Westinghouse, Gibson, Tappan, Kelvinator, Broan, NuTone): 3-letter prefix, then YY (positions 4-5) and MM (positions 6-7), then 5 digits.
sources: Building Intelligence Center - NORDYNE HVAC age (building-center.org/nordyne-hvac-age/)
hvacdecoder.com - Nordyne Serial Number Decoder
howtolookatahouse.com - How can I tell the age of a Nordyne air conditioner from the serial number (2018) - worked example GSD020700023 = July 2002
notes: GSD020700023 = July 2002 is the worked example published by the secondary decoders; the other examples are constructed to the same rule.

Collision: the older Nordyne style puts MM before YY in the same positions (see nordyne-mmyy). When both the YYMM and MMYY readings give a valid month, the era filter decides: MMYY is only used for pre-2000 units. Confirm with the refrigerant on the plate (R-22 = older) and the compressor date code.
Reznor units built after the Nortek acquisition still use the Reznor letter date code, not this format.

serialFormats.description: Older Nordyne style (roughly late 1980s to 1999): 3-letter prefix, then MM (positions 4-5) and YY (positions 6-7), then 5 digits - month and year swapped relative to the current style.
sources: Building Intelligence Center - NORDYNE HVAC age (building-center.org/nordyne-hvac-age/)

notes: LOW confidence: only one secondary source describes the swapped order and its wording is ambiguous about the cutover year (~2000). Treat any pre-2000 Nordyne date as an estimate and confirm from the compressor date code.
Examples are constructed to the rule, not taken from dated plates.
Same regex as nordyne-yymm; the decoder separates them by era and by month validity (a value > 12 in positions 4-5 cannot be a month, so it must be the year).

sequenceOfOperation: Cooling: Y1 (+O) -> board verifies HP/LP/FP1/FP2/CO are normal and the anti-short-cycle timer has expired -> compressor contactor, blower (G) and the accessory (water valve/pump) relay energize; reversing valve energized in cooling.
Heating: Y1 without O -> same sequence with the reversing valve de-energized; FP1 protects the water coil (freeze setpoint 30 F water / 15 F antifreeze selected on the board).

Faults: the board opens the compressor relay, flashes the fault LED and closes the alarm relay; three consecutive faults (retry mode) become a lockout (fast flash) until the Y call or power is cycled.
notes: MEDIUM confidence for HP/LP/FP1/FP2/CO designators and the retry/lockout behaviour (ClimateMaster CXM manual and WaterFurnace Aurora guide summaries); terminal names and the accessory outputs are from builder memory - verify on the board silkscreen and the unit wiring diagram.
Trane Axiom uses different board designations (Deluxe/Basic controls, Tracer ZN524/UC400); this entry is a generic guide only for Axiom.

sequenceOfOperation: Cooling: indoor unit thermo-on sends demand on M-NET -> outdoor unit starts the inverter compressor at minimum frequency after the 3-minute restart delay, ramps to hold target low pressure / evaporating temperature -> LEVs at each indoor unit control superheat -> outdoor fans modulate to hold target high pressure.

Heating: 4-way valve (21S4) energized for heating (City Multi) -> compressor frequency controlled on target condensing temperature -> outdoor LEV controls; defrost by reversing when the outdoor coil thermistor logic demands.
R2 heat recovery: the BC controller solenoid valves route high- or low-pressure gas to each indoor branch per its mode.
notes: LOW confidence: designators from builder memory of City Multi service handbooks; TB3/TB7/63HS/LEV/21S4 naming is standard Mitsubishi practice but was not transcribed from a legend in this review. Confirm on the outdoor unit wiring diagram (inside the control box cover).
Never megger or check continuity on the M-NET line with units powered; disconnect the transmission line before insulation tests.

sequenceOfOperation: Cooling (DX): iCOM enables the main fan continuously; on cooling demand it starts compressor circuit(s) through HP/LP safeties, with head pressure held by the condenser fan speed control or Lee-Temp; unloaders/digital scroll or hot-gas bypass trim capacity on 4-step/variable units.
Dehumidification: compressor runs at reduced airflow/coil temperature and reheat maintains the room temperature; humidification via the canister/infrared humidifier on low-humidity demand.

commonIssues.symptom: Bard wall-mount: unit short-cycles or trips on high pressure in cooling
likelyCauses: Condenser coil fouled (wall-mount coils face outdoors at ground level and load with grass/lint)
checks: Clean the outdoor coil through the front grille
Fan motor amps and run capacitor
Subcooling vs. the charging chart on the unit

commonIssues.symptom: Bard wall-mount with ventilation/economizer package: high humidity or no fresh air, damper stuck
likelyCauses: Economizer/ventilation damper actuator failed or linkage disconnected
checks: Command the damper and watch travel
Verify the ventilation package control inputs per the option's instructions
Filter condition; blower amps

commonIssues.symptom: Reznor / Modine unit heater: venter runs but no ignition, LED 2 flashes
likelyCauses: Pressure switch not proving: blocked vent/flue, cracked tubing, water in the switch, venter wheel dirty
checks: Draft pressure at the switch tap vs. switch rating
Vent termination, screens, ice
Venter motor current and speed
sources: Reznor UDAP/UDAS IOM DSI LED table (2 flashes = pressure switch did not close within 30 s)

commonIssues.symptom: Reznor / Modine unit heater: ignites then locks out (1 flash / ignition lockout)
likelyCauses: Flame sensor dirty or poor burner ground (weak flame current)
Low gas pressure / propane conversion not done
checks: Flame current in microamps; clean the sensor rod
Inlet/manifold pressure during trial
Ground continuity from the burner to the board
sources: Reznor UDAP/UDAS IOM ignition-failure causes list

commonIssues.symptom: Unit heater: burner cycles on limit (3 flashes), discharge very hot
likelyCauses: Fan motor not running / fan relay or time delay failed
checks: Fan starts within the delay after ignition
Manifold pressure and orifice size vs. rating plate
Inspect heat exchanger for cracks / flame rollout
sources: Reznor UDAP/UDAS IOM DSI LED table (3 flashes = limit or rollout open)

commonIssues.symptom: Nordyne / Nortek packaged unit or furnace: intermittent no-heat, control board LED codes
